title: Object authorization and missing subject boundary

threat_model.trust_boundary: Caller identity to object ownership decision
threat_model.failure_mode: A lookup or list operation omits the effective subject or ownership constraint
threat_model.impact: An unauthorized caller may read or mutate an object outside the intended ownership boundary

required_evidence: A protected object is associated with an owner, tenant, seller, or equivalent subject
A caller identity is expected to constrain read or write access to that object

signals: A route or service resolves an object identifier before an ownership decision
A list query can execute without an effective subject predicate
A dictionary-backed object lookup returns an invoice without comparing tenant identity

boundary.subject: effective caller identity
boundary.invariant: Every protected object access is constrained by the effective subject at a canonical enforcement boundary

signals: Trace the effective subject into the canonical object lookup or collection predicate
Compare list, item, bulk, export, and background-job enforcement paths
Compare the role-object-action matrix with the observed enforcement node
Treat null or unresolved identity as evidence to investigate, not as authorization
Use isolated two-subject fixtures and objects owned by each synthetic subject
Assert the foreign object is denied while the owned control remains available

steps: Confirm explicit authorization and create two isolated synthetic subjects
Exercise the owned-object control before the foreign-object comparison
Record response, repository decision, and the enforcement node without using real customer data

false_positive_filters: The route and object are intentionally public under the documented policy
A canonical database or service-layer policy enforces the same subject-object invariant
The suspected path is unreachable from the caller-controlled entrypoint
The observed lookup is a test double that cannot execute in the deployed path

required_evidence: Reachable path from the authorized test entrypoint to the lookup
Observed failed boundary and a safe isolated reproduction
Concrete impact and the defective canonical invariant
refutation_tests: Search for compensating ownership enforcement in lower service, RPC, or database layers
Repeat with an owned object to distinguish general failure from an authorization decision
Reconstruct caller identity resolution without assuming the original hypothesis is correct

root_causes: The effective subject is absent from the canonical data-access contract
Authorization is enforced in presentation code rather than the object boundary
Null or unresolved identity silently widens a protected query

variant_strategy.result_contract: EXACT | VARIANT | REFUTED | BLOCKED; exact and variant matches remain hypotheses until verified

remediation.canonical_invariant: Require the effective subject in the data-access contract and fail closed before every protected object operation
patterns: Use one authorization-aware repository or service boundary for item, list, bulk, and background paths
Keep database row policies or equivalent lower-layer enforcement as defense in depth
Reject missing identity before building a protected query

assertions: The vulnerable control exposes the foreign synthetic object before remediation
The remediated path denies the foreign object and still permits the owned control
List and item paths preserve the same subject-object invariant

calibration.notes: The reference pack has not completed a reproducible benchmark run and makes no precision or recall claim.

limitations: Framework fingerprints are investigation leads and do not establish reachability or impact
Database row policies and service meshes may provide compensating controls outside the reviewed code path
The synthetic fixture proves the contract shape, not performance on external applications
